lab.title: Properties, Backing Fields, and Auto-Properties
lab.objective: Use a backing field only when property access needs custom behavior.
lab.task: Normalize a customer email while keeping a simple loyalty-points property.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/optional/customer-properties from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/optional/customer-properties. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/optional/customer-properties/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Normalize a customer email while keeping a simple loyalty-points property.
Step 4/12: Create sealed CustomerPropertyProfile below the top-level statements.
Step 5/12: Add private string field _email because email assignment needs validation and normalization.
Step 6/12: Add Email with a public getter and private setter.
Step 7/12: Inside the Email setter, reject blank text and store a trimmed lowercase value in _email.
Step 8/12: Add LoyaltyPoints as an auto-property because it needs no custom access behavior.
Step 9/12: Add a constructor that assigns Email so construction follows the same validation path.
Step 10/12: Construct the profile, print both properties, and run the project.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/optional/customer-properties --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/optional/customer-properties --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
